note: Barking is an ongoing sound made by a dog; use a canine subject rather than six human persons.
Lowering a shade, window or setting can be observed in progress; name the object.
An embrace can be underway at a particular moment; the plain present also describes whom one usually hugs.
Mi sto abbronzando describes skin changing in the sun; mi abbronzo facilmente states a tendency.
For where someone lives as a settled fact, use abito; sto abitando would shift toward a temporary arrangement.
Stroking is a repeated gentle movement in progress; identify who is being touched.
Sto accendendo focuses on the short act of switching on; accendo can also describe a routine.
Accepting an offer is an action that can be unfolding; the object identifies what is being accepted.
Accompanying someone lasts through the trip; the person and destination belong together.

A recommendation can be given in an ongoing conversation; the suggestion and recipient are both clear.
Contiene expresses what is inside a container; this relation is not an action unfolding.

Credo expresses a belief held at the moment; a belief forming or changing would need its own reviewed situation.

Cooking is an activity in progress; use a food or meal complement rather than an unrelated generic sentence.

Sto dimagrendo describes weight changing over a period; dimagrisco can also state a tendency.

Relaxing can be unfolding; the reflexive pronoun is part of the Italian verb.

Renewal can be underway through paperwork; the object names what is being renewed.

Sto soffrendo can stress pain or difficulty felt now; soffro il caldo may describe a recurring susceptibility.

sense: be somewhere or feel a certain way
note: Stare in the senses of location and well-being uses sto, stai, sta; progressive stare belongs to another verb’s action, not to this state.

past.en: I felt well during the trip.

simpleExamples.en: Are you staying at home today?

past.en: You used to stay at home every Sunday.
Marco felt unwell that morning.
We were staying here before departure.

note: A single sneeze is brief; sto starnutendo naturally describes a series of sneezes.
Ironing is a task in progress; the clothing item is the direct object.
Studying a subject is a sustained activity; the object or place anchors this session.
Sta succedendo focuses on something occurring now; succede can also report what usually happens.
Sweating continues over a period; the circumstance explains the current physical response.
Playing an instrument has duration; this differs from a bell ringing once.
Mi sto svegliando focuses on the transition from sleep; mi sveglio alle sei gives a daily routine.
Emptying takes several movements; the container is the direct object.
Cutting something into pieces takes time; the object names what is being cut.
A phone call can be in progress; Italian telefonare takes a before its recipient.
Temo expresses fear or concern held; this ordinary attitude is not a process marked with sto temendo.
Holding something can continue over a moment; the physical object is the direct object.
Sto tifando can describe cheering during a match; tifo per names the team one supports generally.
Pulling an object involves force in progress; this sense differs from throwing.
Touching can be sustained as contact; the direct object names what is touched.
Removing an item is a physical action underway; the object says what is being taken away.
Sto tornando presents the trip back as underway; torno can also announce a regular return time.
Coughing can recur over an episode; the manner or setting locates that episode.
Sta tramontando depicts the sun descending now; tramonta alle otto gives a regular or scheduled time.
A household move takes many actions; the destination or circumstances make the current move concrete.
Trembling is an ongoing physical reaction; the cause can be named with di or per.
Trovare in this sense marks successful discovery; sto trovando can instead describe repeated discoveries or solutions emerging.
Putting on make-up takes time; the reflexive points to the person doing their own make-up.
A dive is brief but its movement into water can be seen underway; the reflexive pronoun remains.
Sto ubbidendo can emphasize carrying out an instruction now; ubbidisco can describe general obedience.
Using a device is an action in progress; a named object prevents a vague use.
Sto uscendo focuses on leaving now or imminently; esco can also give a normal departure time.
Vedo expresses perception; watching a film is a deliberate action better taught with guardare, or as a separate sense of vedere.
Selling can be underway as a transaction; the object identifies the item offered.

sense: come toward a person or place
note: Sto venendo can track movement toward the speaker; vengo can also state a plan or repeated visit.
Pouring liquid is a visible action in progress; specify what is poured and where.
Getting dressed is an action underway; the Italian reflexive pronoun changes with the person.
Sto viaggiando focuses on a journey underway; viaggio often states how or where someone habitually travels.
frames: sul treno delle otto e quindici

note: Sto vincendo means the contest is currently going well; it does not assert the final result.
Visiting a site can be underway; this is distinct from the conversational phrase andare a trovare a person.

sense: reside somewhere as a settled fact
note: Vivo gives a usual home or life situation; sto vivendo would add a temporary or actively developing reading that needs its own context.
Flying is a journey underway; volo a Milano can also report an upcoming itinerary.

sense: take a stated amount of time
note: Ci vuole or ci vogliono has an impersonal time or effort subject; this fixed clitic expression states a requirement.

simpleExamples.en: It takes an hour to arrive.

past.en: It used to take an hour to arrive.
It took a lot of patience.

past.it: Ci volevano due giorni per finire.
past.en: It used to take two days to finish.

simpleExamples.en: It takes a lot of money.

past.en: It used to take a lot of money.

note: Voglio states a desire; an ordinary wish is not an action that unfolds as sto volendo.
